finding-your-way.title: Finding your way
finding-your-way.lede: Moving around the app: tiles, the bar at the top, the bar at the side, and going back.

looking-up-words.title: Looking up words
looking-up-words.lede: Finding a word you have just heard: search, which language comes first, other forms, and where the words come from.

reading-a-topic.title: Reading a topic
reading-a-topic.lede: How a topic page is laid out, how its parts are graded, and how to go from one topic to a related one.

your-settings.title: Your settings
your-settings.lede: Changing how the app looks and behaves, and what it keeps on your device.

tiles.title: Tiles
body: The home page shows groups of topics as large tiles. A group opens a page of topic tiles, and a topic opens its words and phrases.
Each tile is a link named in both languages, so a screen reader reads both.
tiles.keys: Tab to a tile, then Enter. The Right arrow also opens the focused tile.

trail.title: Where you are
body: The bar across the top shows where you are, from the home page down to the page you are on. Each step before the last is a link. On wider screens the trail shows both languages.
trail.keys: Tab to a step, then Enter.

side-bar.title: The bar at the side
body: A narrow bar at the side of every page holds the controls. At the top are Search and Back (the home page has no Back). At the bottom are Edit order, About and Settings.
Search and Edit order appear only once the page's script has loaded, and About only where the site has an About page.
side-bar.keys: Tab to a button, then Enter.

back.title: Going back
body: Back goes up one level: from a topic to its group, and from a group to the home page. Settings and About go back to the home page. How to use the app and Sources go back to About.
back.touch: Press the Back arrow in the bar at the side.

pager.title: Reading on
body: At the foot of a topic, two links go to the previous and the next topic, so you can read on without going back up to the group.
pager.keys: Tab to the link, then Enter.

jump-links.title: Jumping to a section
body: A topic with several sections lists them as links under its title. Choose one to go straight to that section.
jump-links.keys: Tab to a section name, then Enter.

keys-and-touch.title: Moving between tiles
body: On a page of tiles you can move from one to the next without a mouse. In a right-to-left language, Right and Left swap.
keys-and-touch.keys: Down arrow and Up arrow move between tiles. Home and End jump to the first and last. Right opens a tile. Left or Backspace goes back.

drag-back.title: Dragging to go back
body: Drag the page towards the end of the line, to the right in a left-to-right language, and the page above it slides in beside it. Let go past about a third of the width, or flick quickly, to go back. Let go early and the page springs back.
A drag that starts at the very edge of the screen is left to your device, so its own back gesture still works. If your device asks for reduced motion, pages do not slide; they simply change.
drag-back.touch: Drag the page to the right and let go.

search.title: Looking up a word
body: Search finds a word or phrase in either language. Type any part of it, in the language you heard or in the other one. Capital letters and accents do not matter: typing without them still finds the word, though a match that keeps them comes first.

Each result shows the word and its translation, with the regional forms side by side, and a link to its row on the page. Under it are links to every topic it appears in. Topics whose title matches what you typed are listed under the words.
The Search button appears only once the page's script has loaded.
search.keys: Press / to open search, or Tab to the Search button and press Enter.
search.touch: Tap the magnifying glass in the bar at the side.

search-keys.title: Moving through results and closing
body: Search stays open while you type. Choose a result to go to it; the card closes as the page changes.
search-keys.keys: Down arrow and Up arrow move through the results. Enter follows the first result when the cursor is in the field. Escape closes search.
search-keys.touch: Tap a result to go to it. Tap Close, or anywhere outside the card, to shut search.

search-this-page-first.title: Results from the page you are on
body: When you open search on a topic, the words found on that page come first. A line headed Other results separates them from the rest. On a group page, the words on all the pages of that group come first. On the home page and other pages there is no such line.

listen-first-rows.title: Which language comes first
body: Each row shows the first language of the pair at the start of the row in large, strong type, and the second language at the end of the same row, in a lighter colour. The first language is the one you hear, so you can scan it quickly. The site chooses the pair.

also-heard.title: Other forms you may hear
body: Under some words a line with a headphones icon lists other forms the word is heard as, such as a changed beginning or a plural. Search finds the word from any of them.

regional-forms.title: Regional forms
body: Some words have different forms in different places. A small tag after a form, such as N or S, shows which region it belongs to; on a computer, pointing at it shows the full name.
In Settings, Regional forms lets you choose a region for a language. Forms that do not belong to it are shown smaller and fainter, and nothing is hidden. The choice is kept on this device.
regional-forms.keys: In Settings, Tab to the choice and use the arrow keys.

sources-notes.title: Notes and sources
body: A small note under a phrase, in lighter type, explains how it is used. Some topics also have a short introduction or a box about a point of grammar, such as a change to the first letter of a word.

The Sources page, linked from About, lists where the phrases come from, the licence each is used under, and how many entries come from each. An entry from an unreviewed draft has not yet been checked against a source.

sections-order.title: How a section is ordered
body: A topic is made of sections, each a card of rows. Under a section's heading, a line beginning Order says how its rows are arranged, for example from lightest to heaviest. Not every section has one.

levels.title: Simple to advanced
body: Tiles and sections are graded from beginner to advanced by what they hold: those with shorter entries are simpler. Nothing is marked on the screen. The grades are used only for the Order choice in Settings, which can put the simplest first or the most advanced first. A screen whose tiles you have arranged yourself keeps your order.

related-topics.title: Linked topics
body: Some topics end with a row of tiles for related topics, so you can go from one to another without going back up. Open one and Back returns you to the topic you came from.
related-topics.keys: Tab to a tile, then Enter, or use the Right arrow.

settings-groups.title: How the settings page is arranged
body: Settings are in groups that open and close when you choose their headings. Only the first group, Accessibility and appearance, starts open.
Settings need scripts to be switched on in your browser. Without them the app follows your device's light or dark setting and uses the default colours.
settings-groups.keys: Tab to a heading, then Enter or Space.

language-toggle.title: Choosing a language
body: Settings, About and the help pages show one language at a time. A toggle at the top right switches between the two. Without the script the first language shows; with it, your last choice is remembered.
language-toggle.keys: Tab to the toggle and use the arrow keys.

view-mode.title: Choosing light or dark
body: View mode has three choices: Same as device, Light and Dark. Same as device follows your device's own light or dark setting.
view-mode.keys: Tab to the choices and use the arrow keys.

accessibility.title: Easier-to-see colour schemes
body: Accessibility chooses which colour schemes are offered below it. Standard shows the usual schemes. Safe colours shows schemes that stay easy to tell apart with colour-blind vision. High contrast shows schemes with stronger text and borders.
Choosing a level switches to the scheme you last picked at that level, or the first it lists.
accessibility.keys: Tab to the choices and use the arrow keys.

colour-schemes.title: Choosing a colour scheme
body: Each colour scheme is shown as a small picture of itself, drawn in its own colours as it would look in the current view mode. Choose one to use it straight away. A level with only one scheme says so.
colour-schemes.keys: Tab to the schemes and use the arrow keys.

order-setting.title: Putting tiles in order
body: Order puts tiles and sections in order: as they are written (Default), the simplest first, or the most advanced first. It applies to the pages you open next. A screen whose tiles you have arranged yourself keeps your own order.
order-setting.keys: Tab to the choices and use the arrow keys.

reset-tile-layouts.title: Putting tiles back
body: Reset tile layouts puts every tile on every page back in its default order. Your appearance and colour choices are kept. The button appears only once the page's script has loaded.
reset-tile-layouts.keys: Tab to the button, then Enter.

what-is-saved.title: What the app remembers
body: Your choices stay on this device and are never sent anywhere. The app remembers your view mode, colour scheme, order, language, regional forms and any tile order you save.
To forget them, clear this site's data in your browser. Reset tile layouts puts only the tiles back.
